description_full: Hello Group Inc. provides mobile-based social and entertainment services in the People's Republic of China and internationally. The company operates in three segments: Momo, Tantan, and QOOL. It offers Momo, a mobile application that connects people and facilitates social interactions based on location, interests, and various online recreational activities, including live talent shows, short videos, as well as other video- and audio-based interactive experiences, such as online parties, mobile karaoke, and user participated reality shows; Tantan, a social and social and dating application; and other applications under the Hertz, Soulchill, Happn, and Duidui names. The company also provides live video services for various content and activities comprising talent shows, short videos as well as other video- and audio-based interactive experiences, such as online parties, mobile karaoke and user participated reality shows; broadcasters and viewers; value-added services; advertising and marketing solutions; and mobile games. The company was formerly known as Momo Inc. and changed its name to Hello Group Inc. in August 2021. Hello Group Inc. was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Beijing, the People's Republic of China.

financial_summary: Hello Group Inc. is a small-cap communication services business with a $635M market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -9% over the past three years, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $104M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.47× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 19× is fortress-like.

Management returns a meaningful 25.9% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Cord-cutting acceleration and audience fragmentation — legacy distribution bundles unravel faster than subscription revenue can replace them.
AI-generated content commoditisation — as creation costs collapse toward zero, content libraries lose pricing power and differentiation narrows.

sect: Its 13% operating margin is roughly in line with the Communication Services median (9%).

mkt: The shares are in a steep downtrend, down 28% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 39% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 29% and a beta of 0.74, it is more defensive than the market.

In past sell-offs it fell 65% in the 2020 crash and 56% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The stock trades 76% below its DCF fair value of $18.57, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 3%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $16.10 to $22.01 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Communication Services peers: P/E 4.6 vs 15.4 and P/FCF 6.1 vs 11.1 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 26% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 16.3% (above the risk-free rate).
The 7 covering analysts target $7.68 on average, 74% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 10% earns above the cost of capital of 8.4%, but the 1pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.38).
It converts 7% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.47x.
ROE of 7% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.3x equity multiplier).
It spends 1.6% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $816.5M (123% of market cap).
growth: Revenue has compounded at -8.6% over 3 years and -7.9% over 5 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 12%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 9.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -25.9% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs 11.1x depreciation (4.8% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and institutions hold 75%.
It returns 25.9% a year to shareholders (17.7% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 4.4% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
people: With about 1,400 employees, each generates about $1.1M of revenue, 1.8x the Communication Services median, and revenue has fallen 4.8% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $74K of free cash flow per employee.
